nina: quick sync: i prototyped an adaptive demote where we blend tenant priors with live samples to avoid aggressive demotes on low-signal tenants. results from a short replay look promising. notes below.

omar: nice. what's the math on the blending?

nina: simple empirical bayes shrinkage: posterior_rate = (alpha * global_rate + n * tenant_rate) / (alpha + n). alpha is the prior strength tuned by tenant size. this gives conservative hotness for small n. pseudocode: 

nina: ```
# on periodic adjudicate
for tenant in tenants:
  n = sketch.sample_count(tenant)
  tenant_rate = sketch.estimate_rate(tenant)
  prior = global_mean_rate
  rate_hat = (alpha + n) > 0 ? (alpha*prior + n*tenant_rate)/(alpha + n) : prior
  budget = budget_fn(rate_hat, tenant_tier)
  for prefix in tenant.active_prefixes:
    rank = sketch.rank(prefix)
    raw_prob = math.max(0, 1 - rank/budget)
    prob = smooth(raw_prob, historical_prob(prefix))
    if rand() < prob and ownership_cache.is_stable(prefix) and now - prefix.last_write_ms > demote_grace_ms:
       soft_demote(prefix, meta={"prob":str(prob)})
```

lee: important that ownership_cache.is_stable(prefix) is fast; otherwise hot path latency suffers. what's the eviction side-effect we saw?

nina: on a 3h replay of multi-tenant traffic we saw token egress reduction ~10%, but some small tenants had a transient 6-8% increase in origin hits when alpha was too small. raising alpha from 20->200 eliminated most spikes.

paul: any correctness regressions? read-after-write guarantees?

nina: none surfaced as client errors. but we observed rare readback patterns where a prefix written < demote_grace_ms was demoted due to stale epoch in the local ownership cache (stale by ~200ms) during a fast handoff.

omar: so race between ownership metadata replication and demote tick. mitigation?

nina: twofold: 1) require ownership_cache.stable_age(prefix) > 500ms in addition to is_stable. 2) critical: we add a tiny soft-pin on recent writes (write_pin_ttl=60s) that prevents demote regardless of prob. that preserves R/W in the common case.

lee: soft-pin TTL seems heavy; can we make it adaptive (shorter for large tenants)?

nina: yes config will be tenant_tier aware. default 60s for small tenants, 10s for enterprise.

paul: operational telemetry we should add: demote_candidate_count, demote_decision_prob, demote_outcome (true/false), demote_bounced_by_pin, demote_bounced_by_ownership. per-tenant tagging.

infra-bot: deploy: rollout plan created -> canary=2 hosts in multi-tenant pool start=2026-03-20T09:00:00Z

nina: logs sample (sanitized):

```
[2026-03-20T09:01:15Z] demote_eval: prefix=cfg_900 tenant=beta prob=0.72 draw=0.61 -> demote (ownership_stable=true)
[2026-03-20T09:01:16Z] rehydrate_cache: miss->origin prefix=cfg_900 tenant=beta latency=72ms
[2026-03-20T09:01:17Z] ownership_cache: refresh prefix=usr_42 state=STABLE age_ms=610
```

omar: good. also add a metric that counts demote->origin read latency and have an alert if demote_to_origin P95 > baseline + 50ms for more than 5m.

nina: will add. testing plan: unit tests for shrinkage math, integration fuzz where we flip epochs mid-demote, and a small canary with sampling alpha variations.

lee: remember to add a deterministic seed mode for replay tests so we can reproduce stochastic failures.

nina: yep - determinism flag available. i'll open the PR today with metrics + ownership_cache guard + tenant_prior paramization. comments welcome.

paul: once PR lands, please pin the alert dashboards and share link. keep the Dedicated pools excluded from initial canary.
